relevance_reason: Functional study explaining why caffeine makes XP-V cells more sensitive to UV, and the role of ATR/Chk1 in replication after UV in cells lacking pol eta.

findings.statement: Using DNA combing, Despras et al. (2010) showed that the translesion synthesis defect in UV-irradiated XP-V cells, which lack DNA polymerase eta, caused a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks. This contrasted with budding yeast. Extensive regions of single-strand DNA formed during replication, and the ATR/Chk1 pathway was over-activated after low UVC doses.
quotes: Using DNA combing, we showed that translesion synthesis defect leads to a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks in human cells, which contrasts with budding yeast.
extensive regions of single-strand DNA are formed during replication in irradiated XP-V cells, leading to an over-activation of ATR/Chk1 pathway after low UVC doses.

findings.statement: Despras et al. (2010) found that adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation lowered Chk1 activation and abolished DNA synthesis in XP-V cells. The Chk1 inhibitor UCN-01 worsened the replication defect in XP-V cells by increasing fork stalling, and like caffeine it made XP-V cells more sensitive to UVC. The authors concluded that pol eta acts at stalled forks to restart them, and that without pol eta, Chk1 becomes essential for replication to resume by alternative pathways through fork stabilization.
quotes: Addition of a low concentration of caffeine post-irradiation, although inefficient to restore S-phase progression, significantly decreases Chk1 activation and abrogates DNA synthesis in XP-V cells.
it aggravates replication defect in XP-V cells by increasing fork stalling. Consequently, UCN-01 sensitizes XP-V cells to UVC as caffeine does.
In the absence of poleta, Chk1 kinase becomes essential for replication resumption by alternative pathways, via fork stabilization.

relevance_reason: Cellular studies showing that pigmented xerodermoid cells cannot be told apart from XP variant cells, and describing the DNA replication defect in XPV.

findings.statement: Cleaver et al. (1980) found that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture could not be told apart from the XP variant in UV-irradiation studies of DNA repair and replication. They concluded that the term 'pigmented xerodermoid', which had been defined by mild clinical symptoms, was therefore redundant.
quotes: It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant and the former term is therefore redundant.
The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms that suggested it might be similar to but distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).

findings.statement: Cleaver et al. (1980) irradiated XP variant and pigmented xerodermoid cells with UV light. They measured unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative replication with or without caffeine, and recovery of DNA replication. The authors concluded that the common defect appeared to be loss of a gene product that lets normal cells replicate DNA without interruption at UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. As a result, replication forks were blocked more often and at lower doses in XP variant cells. They suggested that this defect correlated with the high levels of actinic carcinogenesis seen in these patients.
quotes: The defect common to these cell types appears to be the loss of a gene product that permits normal cells to replicate DNA without interruption at damaged sites (u.v.-induced pyrimidine dimers).
The consequence of this loss is that replication forks are blocked more frequently and at lower doses in XP variant cells.
The correlation between this defect and high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients points to an important role for perturbations in DNA replication in human carcinogenesis.

relevance_reason: Abstract reports cellular diagnostic markers in XPV patients and heterozygous carriers, plus two inherited missense mutations in an XPV family.

findings.statement: Itoh et al. (2000) noted that, among hereditary photosensitive disorders including other XP groups, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome, only XPV cells showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis and normal recovery of RNA synthesis but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation (51 +/- 6% of normal), a reduction enhanced to 36 +/- 5% in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine.
quotes: only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibited normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (51 +/- 6% the rate relative to normal controls)
This reduction of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis was enhanced in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine to 36 +/- 5%.

findings.statement: Itoh et al. (2000) studied 2 independent families with 2 photosensitive patients identified as having XPV. Cells from heterozygous parents showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53 +/- 8% of normal), and normal UV survival without caffeine but slightly reduced survival with caffeine in a colony-forming assay. The authors suggested that XPV heterozygotes can be identified by UV sensitivity in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.
quotes: In this study we assess the cellular markers in two independent families that included two photosensitive patients that were identified as xeroderma pigmentosum variant.

Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, but reduced rates of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53 +/- 8% relative to the normal control).
the cells showed normal survival by ultraviolet without caffeine, but slightly reduced survival by ultraviolet with 1 mM caffeine present.

findings.statement: In 1 family with XPV, Itoh et al. (2000) confirmed inheritance of 2 heterozygous missense mutations: an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 resulting in a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution, and an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 affecting lys589. Neither mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
quotes: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations. One mutation is an A-->G transition at nucleotide 1840 that generates a K535E mis-sense mutation.
Another mutation is an A-->C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that generates a K589 mis-sense mutation. Each of these mutations were absent in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.

relevance_reason: Identifies hRAD30 (POLH) mutations in XP variant cell lines, establishing the causative gene for XPV.

findings.statement: Johnson et al. (1999) found nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of the yeast RAD30 gene, in XP variant (XP-V) cell lines. Of the 8 mutations identified, 7 were predicted to result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein. The authors concluded that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V.
quotes: Here it is shown that XP variant (XP-V) cell lines harbor nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.
Of the eight mutations identified, seven would result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein.
These results indicate that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V

findings.statement: Johnson et al. (1999) noted that yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in error-free bypass of UV damage, and suggested that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.
quotes: Yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in the error-free bypass of ultraviolet (UV) damage.
they suggest that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers

relevance_reason: Identifies DNA polymerase eta as the XPV gene product, reports mutations in all XP-V cells examined, and shows that the recombinant protein corrects the bypass defect in XP-V cell extracts.

findings.statement: Masutani et al. (1999) noted that xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder associated with increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers. Unlike cells from XP groups A to G, XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair but are defective in replicating ultraviolet-damaged DNA.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder which is associated with increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.

Unlike other xeroderma pigmentosum cells (belonging to groups XP-A to XP-G), XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair processes but are defective in their replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA.

findings.statement: Masutani et al. (1999) had used an improved cell-free assay to isolate a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that, in XP-V cell extracts, continued replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers. They showed that this polymerase is a human homolog of yeast Rad30 (DNA polymerase eta). It belongs to a family of damage-bypass replication proteins that also includes E. coli UmuC and DinB and yeast Rev1.
quotes: we have recently isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts
Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.

findings.statement: Masutani et al. (1999) found mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene (POLH) in all XP-V cells they examined. Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrected the inability of XP-V cell extracts to replicate damaged DNA by bypassing thymine dimers. The authors concluded that DNA polymerase eta could be the XPV gene product.
quotes: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrects the inability of XP-V cell extracts to carry out DNA replication by bypassing thymine dimers on damaged DNA.
Together, these results indicate that DNA polymerase eta could be the XPV gene product.

relevance_reason: Describes a diagnostic cellular assay that distinguishes XP variant cells from other photosensitive disorders.

findings.statement: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing xeroderma pigmentosum variant that measures 3 cellular DNA repair markers after UV irradiation: unscheduled DNA synthesis (UDS), recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis. Patient fibroblasts were plated on coverslips alongside normal control cells, and grain counts on nuclei were compared. Among hereditary photosensitive disorders (XP, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome), only XP variant cells showed normal UDS and normal recovery of RNA synthesis but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (about 50% of control), and caffeine made this reduction greater.
quotes: only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibit normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (approximately 50% of that of control cells). This reduction of DNA synthesis is enhanced in the presence of caffeine.

an alternative simple method for the diagnosis of xeroderma pigmentosum variant that measures three cellular markers for DNA repair by autoradiography, unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after ultraviolet irradiation

findings.statement: Itoh et al. (1996) noted that because xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome each produce a different combination of the 3 markers, the method also gives a systematic basis for diagnosing these disorders. Before this method, XP variant had been diagnosed using a post-replication repair assay together with clinical features.
quotes: Because each disorder yields a different combination of these three markers, this method also provides a systematic basis for the diagnosis of these diseases.
Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant have been diagnosed based on a post-replication repair assay using their cells together with their clinical manifestations.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a photosensitive patient (UV81KO) whose cells repair DNA normally but cannot restart DNA synthesis after UV. The authors present this as a new photodermatosis distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum. It is related context for the XP variant entry, not a direct description of XPV.

findings.statement: Fujiwara et al. (1981) described an 8-year-old boy (patient UV81KO) who had only acute recurrent sunburns, with no other physical or neuromental retardation. His skin had lowered minimal erythema doses at monochromatic wavelengths between 280 and 300 nm, without delayed peaking of erythema.
quotes: A non-sensitive, 8-yr-old male patient (termed UV81KO) with only acute recurrent sunburns and without any other physical or neuromental retardations was studied.
The patient's skin exhibited lowered minimal erythema doses between 280 and 300 nm monochromatic wavelengths without delayed peaking of erythema.

findings.statement: Fujiwara et al. (1981) found that the patient's cultured skin fibroblasts were 5-fold more sensitive than normal cells to killing by 254-nm UV, and were also more sensitive to sunlamp UV-B, 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide and N-hydroxy-acetylaminofluorene. The cells were not more sensitive to mitomycin C or to alkylating agents. Cells from obligate heterozygotes responded normally.
quotes: UV81KO skin fibroblasts in culture was 5-fold more sensitive to 254 nm UV killing than normal cells, though the response of obligatory heterozygotes was normal.

UV81KO cells were also more sensitive to killings by fluorescent sunlamp (295-300 nm UV-B) radiation, 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide, and N-hydroxy-acetyl aminofluorene, but not by monofunctional decarbamoyl mitomycin C, bifunctional mitomycin C, and alkylating agents

findings.statement: Fujiwara et al. (1981) found no detectable defect in nucleotide excision repair or replicative bypass in the patient's cells. Despite this, the cells failed to recover DNA synthesis after 254-nm UV doses of 1 and 5 J/m2, doses at which normal cells recovered. Baseline sister chromatid exchanges were raised (10 to 12 per cell versus 5 per cell in normal cells), but the rate of UV-induced exchanges was normal.
quotes: indicated no apparently detectable defects in nucleotide-excision repair processes and in replicative bypass in UV81KO cells.
Despite the repair proficiency as such, UV81KO cells showed the defective recovery of DNA synthesis after 254 nm UV irradiation with 1 and 5 J/m2, at which dose the recovery occurred in normal cells.
The base line level of sister-chromatid exchanges (SCEs) was higher in UV81KO cells (10-12 SCEs/cell) than in normal cells (5 SCEs/cell)

findings.statement: Fujiwara et al. (1981) compared the patient's features with those of xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, the 11961 disorder and Bloom syndrome. They concluded that the UV81KO disorder was distinct from all of these and proposed it as a new photodermatosis with a defect in the recovery of DNA synthesis after UV exposure.
quotes: Such clinical, cellular and molecular characteristics and comparison to those in the other photodermatoses (xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne's syndrome, the 11961 disorder, Bloom's syndrome) can make a clear distinction of UV81KO from the others.
Thus, the UV81KO disorder is put forward as a new photodermatosis with a defect in the recovery of post-UV DNA synthesis.

relevance_reason: The title describes xeroderma pigmentosum variants with normal DNA repair, which is the defining feature of this entry (XP, variant type). Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Cleaver (1972) described variants of xeroderma pigmentosum that had normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a review of xeroderma pigmentosum in general (sun sensitivity, multiple skin cancers, abnormal DNA repair), with no stated details about the variant form specifically.

findings.statement: Robbins et al. (1974) described xeroderma pigmentosum as an inherited disease with sun sensitivity, multiple cutaneous neoplasms, and abnormal DNA repair.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum. An inherited diseases with sun sensitivity, multiple cutaneous neoplasms, and abnormal DNA repair.

relevance_reason: A functional study of UV-induced mutagenesis in XP variant cells, using a shuttle vector plasmid. It gives a mechanism for why these cells are hypermutable.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (1991) stated that patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show the clinical features of XP, including more frequent skin cancer. Their cells have a normal or nearly normal rate of nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA damage. The cells are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV radiation but are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) variant patients show the clinical characteristics of the disease, with increased frequencies of skin cancer, but their cells have a normal, or nearly normal, rate of nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA damage
are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV radiation. However, they are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (1991) transfected an XP variant cell line with a supF shuttle vector plasmid irradiated with UV at 254 nm. Mutant frequency rose linearly with dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than previously seen in normal cells. In 52 of 53 independent mutants the change was a base substitution, and 62 of 64 substitutions involved a dipyrimidine. A.T base pairs were involved in 28% of mutations in XP variant cells versus 11% in normal cells, mostly at position 136. The authors suggested that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite photoproducts, which could account for their UV hypermutability.
quotes: The frequency of mutants increased linearly with dose, but with a slope 5 times steeper than that seen with normal cells.

52 of 53 independent mutants generated in the XP variant cells contained base substitutions, with 62 of 64 of the substitutions involving a dipyrimidine. Twenty-eight percent of the mutations involved A.T base pairs, with the majority found at position 136
our data suggest that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite bases involved in photo-products.

relevance_reason: Defines the cellular defect of the XP variant: normal excision repair but defective post-UV DNA synthesis (postreplication repair), which is caffeine-sensitive.

findings.statement: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that cells from the class of xeroderma pigmentosum patients whose excision repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers was completely normal (XP variants) had an abnormality in DNA synthesis after UV irradiation. These variant cells took much longer than normal cells to convert the low-molecular-weight DNA first made after UV irradiation into high-molecular-weight DNA.
quotes: There is, however, one class of these patients whose cells are completely normal in this excision repair process. We have found that these cells have an abnormality in the manner in which DNA is synthesized after UV-irradiation.

The time taken to convert initially low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized in UV-irradiated cells into high-molecular-weight DNA similar in size to that in untreated cells is much greater in these variants than in normal cells.

phenotypes.text: normal excision repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers
defective DNA synthesis after UV irradiation

findings.statement: Lehmann et al. (1975) showed that caffeine strongly inhibited the slow conversion of newly made low-molecular-weight DNA to high-molecular-weight DNA in UV-irradiated XP variant cells, but had no effect in normal cells. Two excision-repair-deficient XP cell lines showed intermediate effects, both in the time needed for this conversion and in how much caffeine inhibited it.
quotes: Furthermore, this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.

Two cell lines from classes of xeroderma pigmentosum that are defective in excision-repair show intermediate effects, with regard to both the time taken to convert newly synthesized DNA to high molecular weight and the inhibition of this process by caffeine.
